unit.why: A short narrative: the Seer of Lublin, reading the kvittel of the child R. Asher Yeshaya of Ropshitz, called him 'a nice little Passover sacrifice'; the meaning became clear only when he died on Passover eve 1845.

stories.start_quote: וככה הי' גם עם מחו׳ הרה"ק
stories.summary_en: When R. Asher Yeshaya of Ropshitz was a child, the Seer of Lublin read his kvittel and called him 'a nice little Passover offering'. This was understood only in retrospect, when he died on the eve of Passover 1845.

quotes: אמר עליו א שיין קרבן פסחיל
tags.why: The Seer's remark foretold the day of his death.
The story's whole arc is a prediction that comes true.

quotes: אז ראו למפרע את אשר חזו עיני קודש
tags.why: The meaning of the remark was understood only later.

quotes: אשר חזו עיני קודש הרבי מלובלין
tags.why: The Seer foresaw the future through holy insight.

quotes: עד יום פטירת האי סבא קדישא
tags.why: The tzaddik's death is the event that fulfils the prediction.
The death falls on Passover eve, which gives the remark its meaning.
The Seer reads the child's kvittel, as at an audience.

quotes: אשר מילא מקום חותנו רבינו הקדוש
tags.why: He is presented as the son-in-law and successor of R. Naftali of Ropshitz, and as a relative of the narrator.

quotes: אשר מילא מקום חותנו רבינו הקדוש מו"ה נפתלי צבי
tags.why: His succession to his father-in-law is mentioned only in passing.

missing_concepts: kvittel (petition note) read by the tzaddik
